title: Finite internal normalization separates two nonlocal join centers
statement: Let $P$ be a normal integral domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] with fraction field $K$, fix a separable closure $K^{\mathrm{sep}}/K$ [def-kun-separably-closed], and choose $P$-embeddings $H_i=P^h_{\mathfrak q_i}\hookrightarrow K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ for two primes $\mathfrak q_i\subset P$ [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime]. Let $J\subset K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ be the subring generated by the $H_i$, and let $L=\operatorname{Frac}(J)$. Suppose $J$ is a normal henselian local domain [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and both maps $H_i\to J$ are nonlocal, meaning that their inverse images of $\mathfrak m_J$ are proper subideals of $\mathfrak m_{H_i}$. There exist a finite separable field extension $K\subseteq K_0\subseteq L$ (finite-dimensional as a $K$-vector space), its integral closure $P_0=\{x\in K_0:x\text{ satisfies a monic polynomial over }P\}$, and primes $\mathfrak q_{0,i}\subset P_0$ over $\mathfrak q_i$, such that $P_0$ is a normal domain with fraction field $K_0$, neither $\mathfrak q_{0,1}\subseteq\mathfrak q_{0,2}$ nor $\mathfrak q_{0,2}\subseteq\mathfrak q_{0,1}$, and there are compatible embeddings $P_{0,\mathfrak q_{0,i}}^h\hookrightarrow J\subset K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ extending the embeddings of $H_i$. The two enlarged henselizations generate exactly $J$.

source.place: Agent-formulated internal-normalization refinement of the normalized-center comparison in the proof of Theorem 6.3, printed p. 13. The field K_0 is chosen inside Frac(J), not an arbitrary finite subextension of the ambient separable closure. The proof obligations concerning the centers and compatible enlarged henselizations are the content of this auxiliary node; they are not asserted to be elementary or to be the literal statement of Theorem 6.3. Online source read; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Inside $L$ put $B=\operatorname{icl}_P(L)$ and $S_i=\operatorname{icl}_{H_i}(L)$, the integral closures of [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Each $S_i$ is a nonzero domain as a subring of $L$, so its only idempotents are $0,1$: $e(e-1)=0$ forces one factor to vanish. It is integral over $H_i$ by construction. Apply [lem-trf-integral-component-henselian-permanence] to obtain that $S_i$ is henselian local and $H_i\to S_i$ is local.

source.place: Construction of the individual normalizations; more-algebra.tex Tag 092X (lemma-integral-over-henselian), domain case of the cited permanence statement.

proof.text: Every $s\in S_i$ satisfies a monic equation over $H_i\subseteq J$, hence over $J$. Since $s\in L=\operatorname{Frac}(J)$, normality of $J$ in [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] gives $S_i\subseteq J$. Every monic equation over $P$ is also one over $H_i$, so $B\subseteq S_i$. Define the prime $\mathfrak r_i=B\cap\mathfrak m_{S_i}$; then $\mathfrak r_i\cap P=\mathfrak q_i$, because $P_{\mathfrak q_i}\to H_i\to S_i$ is local.

source.place: Agent monic-equation and prime-contraction calculation; henselization locality is the stated universal-property convention, Tag 04GQ.

proof.text: The ring $B$ is a normal domain with fraction field $L$. Indeed $L/K$ is algebraic, since $L\subseteq K^{\mathrm{sep}}$. For $x\in L$, take $x^n+\sum_{j<n}c_jx^j=0$ over $K$ and a common nonzero denominator $d\in P$ for its coefficients. Then $dx$ satisfies $T^n+\sum_{j<n}d^{n-j}c_jT^j=0$ over $P$, so $dx\in B$ and $x=(dx)/d$. Thus $\operatorname{Frac}(B)=L$. If $x\in L$ is integral over $B$, let $C=\operatorname{icl}_B(L)$. By [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], both $P\to B$ and $B\to C$ are integral. [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive] makes $x\in C$ integral over $P$, hence $x\in B$. The criterion in [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] proves normality.

source.place: Agent denominator calculation and Tag 00GN (lemma-integral-transitive); analogous denominator calculation in Tag 00GY (lemma-localize-normal-domain).

proof.text: Fix $i$. By [lem-trf-henselization-prime-ind-etale] and [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], write $H_i$ as a filtered colimit of etale $P$-algebras $E_\alpha$. Every $h\in H_i$ is the image of some $e\in E_\alpha$, by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise]. Put $\mathfrak t_\alpha=(E_\alpha\to S_i)^{-1}(\mathfrak m_{S_i})$. The map $P\to E_\alpha$ is finite type and quasi-finite at this prime by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-quasi-finite]. Let $C_\alpha$ be the integral closure of $P$ in $E_\alpha$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-zariski-main-away] to get $g\in C_\alpha\setminus\mathfrak t_\alpha$ with $(C_\alpha)_g\xrightarrow{\sim}(E_\alpha)_g$. This applies to $E_\alpha$ itself; no assertion that its image in $L$ is etale is used.

source.place: Tags 04GN/04GV (lemma-henselization / lemma-henselization-different), 00U5 (lemma-etale-quasi-finite), and 00Q9 (theorem-main-theorem), applied at the contracted prime of an actual etale stage.

proof.text: The isomorphism in Step 4 writes $e/1=c/g^n$ for some $c\in C_\alpha$ and $n\geq0$. Map this equality into $L$ through $E_\alpha\to H_i\subseteq S_i$: the image $\bar g$ is outside $\mathfrak m_{S_i}$, hence nonzero. The elements $\bar c,\bar g$ satisfy the images of their monic equations over $P$, so belong to $B$ by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]; moreover $\bar g\notin\mathfrak r_i$. Thus $h=\bar c/\bar g^n\in B_{\mathfrak r_i}$. This proves $H_i\subseteq B_{\mathfrak r_i}$. Conversely $B\subseteq S_i$ and every element of $B\setminus\mathfrak r_i$ is a unit of $S_i$, giving $B_{\mathfrak r_i}\subseteq S_i$ as subrings of $L$.

source.place: Agent evaluation of the fractions supplied by Tag 00Q9; denominators are outside the specified branch prime, so the localization map into S_i exists.

proof.text: By Step 3 and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain], $B_{\mathfrak r_i}$ is a normal domain with fraction field $L$. Every $s\in S_i$ lies in $L$ and satisfies a monic equation over $H_i\subseteq B_{\mathfrak r_i}$. The normal-domain criterion [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] therefore gives $s\in B_{\mathfrak r_i}$. Together with Step 5 this proves the actual equality $S_i=B_{\mathfrak r_i}$ inside $L$, for both indices.

source.place: Tag 00GY (lemma-localize-normal-domain), followed by the defining monic-root criterion. This derives the branch comparison instead of citing the withdrawn branch auxiliary.

proof.text: The primes $\mathfrak r_1,\mathfrak r_2$ are incomparable. If $\mathfrak r_1\subseteq\mathfrak r_2$, taking complements and fractions gives $B_{\mathfrak r_2}\subseteq B_{\mathfrak r_1}$, hence $S_2\subseteq S_1$. Then $S_1$ contains both $H_1,H_2$, hence their generated ring $J$. Step 2 gives $S_1\subseteq J$, so $S_1=J$. But $H_1\to S_1$ is local by Step 1, contrary to the given nonlocal map $H_1\to J$. Interchanging the indices excludes $\mathfrak r_2\subseteq\mathfrak r_1$.

source.place: Agent comparison of the two explicitly identified localizations; this uses their own maximal ideals, not the contraction of m_J.

proof.text: Choose $a\in\mathfrak r_1\setminus\mathfrak r_2$ and $b\in\mathfrak r_2\setminus\mathfrak r_1$. Put $K_0=K(a,b)\subseteq L$. Each generator is separable algebraic over $K$ since it lies in $K^{\mathrm{sep}}$. If their equation degrees are $d,e$, then the powers $a^u b^v$ with $u<d,v<e$ span $K[a,b]$. This is a finite-dimensional domain over $K$; multiplication by a nonzero element is injective, hence surjective, so it is a field. Consequently $K[a,b]=K_0$ is finite separable over $K$. Put $P_0=B\cap K_0$ and $\mathfrak q_{0,i}=\mathfrak r_i\cap P_0$. These primes contract to $\mathfrak q_i$ by Step 2. Both $a,b$ lie in $P_0$ and witness the two failures of inclusion between the $\mathfrak q_{0,i}$.

source.place: Agent finite-witness construction inside L; separability is inherited from the given separable closure and finiteness is proved by the explicit span.

proof.text: The ring $P_0=B\cap K_0$ is exactly the integral closure of $P$ in $K_0$ by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Repeat the denominator calculation of Step 3 for $x\in K_0$: a monic relation over $K$ and a common nonzero denominator $d\in P$ give a monic relation for $dx$, so $dx\in P_0$ and $x=(dx)/d$. Thus $\operatorname{Frac}(P_0)=K_0$. Let $C_0=\operatorname{icl}_{P_0}(K_0)$. Both $P\to P_0$ and $P_0\to C_0$ are integral, so [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive] makes every $x\in C_0$ integral over $P$, whence $x\in P_0$. Therefore $P_0$ is normal by [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. No claim that $P_0$ is a finite $P$-module is needed.

source.place: Agent denominator calculation; Tag 00GN (lemma-integral-transitive). This uses algebraicity of K_0/K, not finiteness of a normalization module.

proof.text: Put $R_i=(P_0)_{\mathfrak q_{0,i}}$. It is a normal local domain with fraction field $K_0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain]. The inclusion $P_0\subseteq S_i$ extends to an injective local map $R_i\to S_i$: a denominator outside $\mathfrak q_{0,i}=P_0\cap\mathfrak m_{S_i}$ becomes a unit, and the inverse image of $\mathfrak m_{S_i}$ consists exactly of fractions with numerator in $\mathfrak q_{0,i}$. Let $H_{0,i}=R_i^h$. The universal property [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime], with henselian local target $S_i$, supplies a unique local map $\phi_i:H_{0,i}\to S_i$ extending this inclusion. Injectivity of $\phi_i$ will be proved below.

source.place: Tag 00GY and the henselization universal property Tag 04GQ; locality is into S_i and is not asserted for S_i -> J.

proof.text: Fix $i$ and abbreviate $R=R_i$, $H=H_{0,i}$. Since $R$ is local, $R_{\mathfrak m_R}=R$ (all denominators are units); uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime] identifies $H$ with its henselization at $\mathfrak m_R$. Thus [lem-trf-henselization-prime-ind-etale] and [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra] give a filtered etale presentation $H=\varinjlim E_\alpha$ over $R$. Every prime localization of the normal domain $R$ is normal by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain]. Hence $R$ is a normal ring, and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-colimit-normal-local-domain] applies: $H$ is a normal domain and $R\to H$ is injective.

source.place: More on Algebra Tag 06DI (lemma-henselization-normal), in its already existing etale-colimit formulation; Algebra Tags 04GN and 00GY check its hypotheses.

proof.text: Let $F=\operatorname{Frac}(R)=K_0$ and $G=\operatorname{Frac}(H)$, with $F\subseteq G$ by Step 11. For $x\in H$, [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] chooses $e\in E_\alpha$ mapping to $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change], $F\otimes_R E_\alpha$ is etale over $F$, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product] expresses it as a finite product of finite separable field extensions $F_j/F$. The map $F\otimes_R E_\alpha\to G$, $c\otimes e\mapsto c\bar e$, is unital, so this product is nonzero. In each $F_j$ the coordinate of $1\otimes e$ satisfies a nonzero monic polynomial $p_j(T)\in F[T]$. Their product is nonzero and annihilates every coordinate, and therefore its image $x$ in $G$. This proves that every $x\in H$ is algebraic over $F$.

source.place: Tags 00U2 (lemma-etale), base change, and 00U3 (lemma-etale-over-field), finite product of finite separable extensions; the annihilating polynomial is constructed coordinate by coordinate.

proof.text: The maps $P_{\mathfrak q_i}\to R_i\to H_{0,i}$ are local because $\mathfrak q_{0,i}\cap P=\mathfrak q_i$. By [def-weil-pbc-henselization-at-prime] there is a unique local map $u_i:H_i\to H_{0,i}$ extending $P_{\mathfrak q_i}\to R_i$. Both $\phi_i u_i$ and the original $H_i\to S_i$ are local maps extending the same $P_{\mathfrak q_i}\to S_i$, so the same universal property gives $\phi_i u_i=(H_i\to S_i)$. This proves compatibility with the prescribed embeddings in $K^{\mathrm{sep}}$. The right-hand side is injective, so $u_i$ is injective as well. Uniqueness is applied only with target $S_i$, where locality was established.

source.place: Tag 04GQ (definition-henselization), applied twice with local maps into the specified henselian targets.

proof.text: Let $J_0\subseteq K^{\mathrm{sep}}$ be generated by the two images of $H_{0,i}$. Step 13 gives $J_0\subseteq J$. Step 14 says that these images contain the two given $H_i$, so they contain the ring $J$ generated by them. Hence $J_0=J$. Together with Steps 8--9 and the compatible embeddings from Steps 13--14, this is every clause of the unchanged statement.

proof_origin.place: Explicit application of Zariski Main to etale stages of the two henselizations, followed by normality and a generic polynomial kernel calculation. All non-elementary inputs are existing cited nodes; the internal refinement is not stated in Huebner--Schmidt Theorem 6.3.

split_report.summary: Repair of E1/E3 and D1: retain the item statement verbatim; withdraw both Artin-clause drafts and both later branch/lift auxiliaries. Derive the branch comparison directly from existing henselization, etale quasi-finiteness and Zariski Main nodes. Prove injectivity by normality, the existing etale-over-field decomposition and an explicit nonzero-constant-term polynomial calculation. The finite witnesses lie in Frac(J), the embeddings land in the individual normalizations inside J, and exact generation follows by two containments. Fifteen steps, no new nodes.
